title: Minimum Absolute Distance Between Mirror Pairs
summary: Given an integer array, find the minimum absolute difference between indices of any pair where the first index's number reversed equals the second index's number.
statement: Given an integer array, find the minimum absolute difference between indices of any pair where the first index's number reversed equals the second index's number. If no such pair exists, return -1.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 positive integers.
A pair i<j qualifies when reversing decimal nums[i] (dropping leading zeros) equals nums[j].
Return the minimum j-i, or negative one when no directional pair exists.
hints: Scanning left to right handles the required direction i<j.
Map each reversed earlier value to the latest index that is waiting for that future value.
At index j, look up nums[j], update the minimum gap, then register reverse(nums[j]).
The latest matching producer always gives the smallest gap ending at j, and every directional pair is checked at its endpoint.
editorial: The latest matching producer always gives the smallest gap ending at j, and every directional pair is checked at its endpoint.

tests.explanation: Pairs 12→21 and 45→54 have gaps one and two, so the minimum is one.
Reversing the earlier 120 gives the later 21 at distance one.
